functional_description: phenotype-preserving rewriting of the genetic system that changes the distribution of offspring phenotypes available to subsequent search, without changing the current phenotype
mechanism: apply an operator to a sequence
inverse-apply an operator to a sequence
delete an operator, only if never applied during ontogenesis
apply an operator to all sequences then delete it
create a new operator from a random subsequence of stochastic length 2 + Poisson(1), then inverse-apply it
control_parameter: beta, the Poisson mean number of such rewrites per genotype per reproduction
ablation_available: yes, beta = 0 removes the mechanism entirely and freezes the encoding as a direct one
historical_evidence_of_effect: fitness trajectories differ sharply between arms, and at high mutation rate the ablated arm never converges (SRC-PHD-2003 Figure 1.7)
historical_evidence_on_accessibility: NONE. The claim that the mechanism 'changed the exploration distribution' is asserted in the prose of section 1.5.4 and was never measured in that experiment.
note: This row is a candidate only. It is promoted to a part if and only if HC-T01 shows the mechanism alters the detector trajectory beyond the mechanical-effect null AND that this relates to subsequent acquisition.
